text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident alert: hosted-api service exceeded 2% 5xx for 5m (rule High5xxRate). Paging oncall.
Alex Chen: I'm on it. Seeing a spike in tail latency for model-serving-03, looks like KV cache misses are spiking.
Alex Chen: quick check — rolling restart of a subset helped last time. Can we confirm which pool is impacted? @Sam Patel can you pull the per-pool error/latency?

Sam Patel: pulling dashboards now -> https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ABCD/hosted-api-overview?orgId=1&from=now-30m&to=now

Sam Patel: per-pool view: model-serving-03 (us-east-1-g4) has 2.6% 5xx, cpu ~85%, batch queue length increased. Other pools normal.

Tia Ramirez: paging noise is high, multiple followups from integrations team. Any customer-facing errors? CS reported increased 500s for a handful of orgs.

Alex Chen: Confirmed customer impact: a handful of requests failing with 502 from proxy. Not all customers, looks tied to certain prompt length distribution hitting long sequences.

Maria Gonzalez: Thanks. Two parallel asks: (1) Live mitigation to reduce customer impact, (2) Post-incident tuning to reduce pager noise. For live: do a canary restart of model-serving-03 hosts with a short drain window and add temporary circuit-breaker to degrade to smaller model variant for long sequences.

Alex Chen: Doing canary restart now on 3 nodes. Command:

```
# drain one node
curl -X POST https://api.internal/hosts/drain -d '{"host":"ms-03-42"}'
# restart service
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/model-serving-03
```

ops-bot: Deploy started by Alex Chen for model-serving-03. Rollout controller reports 3/8 pods restarted.

Alex Chen: After first node restart latency down slightly. 5xx from 2.6% -> 1.8% in last 2m. Continuing canary.

Sam Patel: Noted. Long-term we should tune the alert: it currently pages for any >2% across any 5m window. That threshold is too sensitive for noisy transient loads. Propose: change to 3m window and 3% threshold for page, keep 1.5% for ticket.

Maria Gonzalez: Agreed. Also adjust routing: only page to #eng-oncall when service=hosted-api AND affected_customers>5 OR severity=high. Otherwise open ticket in #eng-sre-alerts. That will cut down noise.

Michael Li: small caveat: some high-revenue customers may need immediate paging even if only 1 customer affected. We need label-based routing (customer_tier=premium) to still page.

Alex Chen: Good point. Implementation plan:
- Live: finish canary and add short-term circuit-breaker for sequence_length>1024 to fallback to smaller model for 15 minutes.
- Postmortem action items: update alert rules, add dashboard for per-customer 5xx, implement routing policy change with premium-customer override, add runbook note for draining/restart.

Tia Ramirez: For the alert rule change, here's a suggested Prometheus snippet. Please review before I push change.

```
alert: High5xxRate
expr: |
  sum by (service) (rate(requests_total{status=~"5..",service="hosted-api"}[3m]))
  / sum by (service) (rate(requests_total{service="hosted-api"}[3m])) > 0.03
for: 3m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  runbook: https://confluence.redwood/internal/runbooks/high5xx
```

Maria Gonzalez: I like that as a starting point. Also add a sibling rule for 'High5xxTicket' with severity: ticket and threshold 0.015 over 5m. Then route tickets to #eng-sre-alerts and pages to #eng-oncall with additional matching for customer count/premium label.

Sam Patel: I'll create the dashboard panel for per-customer 5xx (by org_id) and a short-lived alert that triggers an internal metric when affected_customers_count>5. That metric will be used in routing.

Alex Chen: Canary finished. Metrics trending down: 5xx now at 0.9% across hosted-api. Rolling complete. Circuit-breaker in place for long sequences for 15m. Customer reports dropping.

Tia Ramirez: Confirmed CS reported reduced errors for affected orgs. Closing the pager for this incident. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident closed by Alex Chen. Duration 18m. Automation created incident-1745604321 in incidents tracker.

Maria Gonzalez: I'll own the post-incident followups. Action items for next 48h:
- Sam: dashboard and affected_customers metric (owner)
- Tia: update runbook text and add guidance for when to escalate to premium-customer page (owner)
- Alex: PR for alert threshold/routing change, include examples for label-based overrides (owner)
- Michael: confirm enterprise SRE team notified for any premium-customer blips (owner)

Michael Li: I'll sync with enterprise SRE and make sure the premium override list is up-to-date.

Alex Chen: Quick note: when we change routing, let's set a soft window (no auto-paging for 24h after change) and monitor for missed regressions. We should also add a dashboard alert to notify if routing drop causes under-notification (i.e., customers impacted but no page).

Maria Gonzalez: Agreed. I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up sync tomorrow 10:00am to review the PR and dashboards. Meeting invite will be in #eng-sre.

Alex Chen: TL;DR: mitigated with canary restart + circuit-breaker, customers largely recovered, follow-ups to harden alerts and routing to reduce noise while preserving premium-customer pages. Thanks everyone.

ops-bot: Reminder: please attach postmortem links and publish within 5 business days."
